messages:
emma: Quick follow-up on the service fission RFC — proposal to split inference-surface into a hotpath (low-latency token gen) and an enrichment-slowpath (post-processing, batch jobs). Need to decide KV cache ownership and a rollout cadence. Thoughts?

raj: Key tradeoff is cache locality vs operational surface. If we centralize the KV cache we add cross-service latency; if we keep it with hotpath we preserve latency but complicate migration and multi-tenant isolation.

olivia: Central Redis cluster is simplest from a code perspective but I'm worried about cost and blast radius. Sidecar per-tenant avoids cross-tenant noise but is heavier ops.

mike: Sidecar is appealing for Dedicated customers. Hosted multi-tenant sidecars seem heavy. Could do sidecar for Dedicated, central for hosted.

lia: What about a hybrid: hotpath keeps a tiny local LRU for immediate tokens; slowpath (enrichment) reads from a central store for misses. That reduces cross-service sync while keeping p99 low. Need to define cache semantics though (staleness ok?).

emma: Draft proposal: 1) Define a minimal cache contract (getMany/put/bulk TTL semantics). 2) Build a sidecar prototype and canary on Dedicated customers. 3) Implement a central read-through fallback for hosted. 4) Migrate via feature flag, with automatic fallback on memory/latency alarms. Example contract snippet: 
```
// cache contract
get(keys: string[]) -> {hits: Record<string,string>, misses: string[]}
put(kv: Record<string,string>, ttl_ms?: number) -> ok
```

raj: Agree. Add automatic fallback rules: if sidecar mem_rss > X or p99_cache_lookup > Y ms, route to central. Also record metrics: hit_rate, p99_latency, mem_rss per sidecar, and inter-service latency.

olivia: +1 on metrics. Who will own the canary runbook and SLIs? :thumbsup:

mike: Infra will own sidecar infra (deployment, autoscaling). Runtime team owns the contract and correctness tests. Product/solutions owns rollout criteria and customer comms.

emma: Timeline? Targeting early next quarter: spike in sprint 1 (prototype + contract), sprint 2 (sidecar canary + central fallback), sprint 3 (broader rollout). Can we map two sprint milestones for MVP?

lia: I'll draft the runbook and the test matrix (unit tests, integration with runtime, load test with 90/10 hotpath/slowpath mix). @infra-bot can we get a canary cluster allocated?

infra-bot: Created cluster redwood-canary-cache-03 in us-west-2. Labels: team=canary, purpose=cache-sidecar.

emma: Thanks — I'll post a short RFC follow-up doc with the hybrid recommendation and owners. Any objections to the hybrid approach as the initial strategy?

raj: No objections, small ask: we should quantify cost delta for sidecar vs central in the doc. I'll follow up with a cost sketch.

olivia: Also add a rollback checklist: feature-flag off, TTL backfill, and customer-notify steps.

emma: Perfect — I'll integrate runbook, owners, and rollback checklist into the doc and tag reviewers.

mike: One more operational note: ensure sidecar image has small memory budget defaults (256-512MB) and explicit metrics export for autoscaler.

lia: I'll include mem defaults and tests.

emma: Great work team — I'll assign action items in the RFC follow-up. Closing thread for now. :rocket:
